verdict:
Yes, but only with the three commits of this review on top: merge 458a03aef (branch review-stage1c-m2-validity-2), not edd147a7e as it was delivered.

The commit under review returns a wrong reduced model at default options and in primal-only mode on two models that I built, and on 178 of a family of 1,500 such models. The cause is one: the forcing test that simple probing shares with the forcing row allows a gap of "rounding size" measured in units of the sum of the terms of the row and of the error bound of its activity. A continuous column with a small coefficient may then sit far more than rounding off the bound that its alias puts it on, and a row that holds the column with a large coefficient is moved by 3.5e-3 (first model) or 2.5e-5 (second model). The base engine is right on both models, the structure check is silent on both wrong results, and the campaign cannot draw them.

Commit 2272aaac7 repairs the rule (a test of that slack against the largest coefficient of the column, option probing_slack), commit ceb56c208 adds eleven wrong engines. With them the rule is right on both models and on the family, and nothing is lost: on the 240 and the 17 local dumps every field of the tool's result but the seconds equals the commit under review, in default and primal-only mode.

Commit 458a03aef repairs the same allowance where it comes from, in the forcing row of Stage 1: the base commit fa8430e24 reports a feasible model infeasible there (new class, not one of the known three). It is a strict tightening and changes nothing on the 17 and 240 dumps or on 4.2 million random models, but it is Stage 1 code. It is separable: ceb56c208 is milestone M2 with its own repair alone and carries the full-size campaign; 458a03aef carries a shorter one (51 million release and 25.5 million assertion models).

Everything else I attacked held: the preconditions of the design are in the code and tested on the state of the call, the moved doubleton code does what it did, identity with the family off, fixed points, the 110 wrong engines of the author.

Columns: p binary with cost 1; x1 continuous in [0, 4e5 + 6 ulp(4e5)]; x2 continuous in [0, 1]; z continuous in [0, 2]. Rows: A: (4e7 + 100) p + 100 x1 + 100 x2 = 4e7 + 100; B1: 1e7 x2 + 1e7 z <= 1e7 (2 - 6 ulp); B2: 1e7 x2 - 1e7 z <= 0. NOT A WRONG RESULT by the engine's tolerance, reported because the task asks for every model on which the rule's conditions change the feasible set in exact arithmetic. The design accepts a gap within the forcing tolerance; a negative gap (the conditional row has no point at all) counts as forcing, also next to a continuous column. Model: 2 p + x1 + x2 = 2, x1 continuous in [0, 1 - 3e-7], x2 binary, min p. Exact: only p = 1, x1 = x2 = 0, optimum 1. The engine makes x1 = (1 - 3e-7)(1 - p), x2 = 1 - p and deletes the row; the reduced model keeps p = 0, which postsolves to a point with the row off by 3e-7 (optimum 0). The integer form: 2 p + x + y = 2 + 4e-7 with binaries has no exact point and is reduced to a feasible model. The same convention as the forcing row and every redundancy test of Stage 1. With exact gaps (zero) the conditions leave the feasible set and the optimum unchanged on 16,662 applications by hand.
other_defects: Weak checks on the two wrong results of the rule: the structure check is silent on both (a wrong alias whose row composes to 0 = 0 is a restriction, which it cannot see by design), and the campaign can neither draw nor judge them: the oracle class has one continuous column per row and the oracle reads a row with a relative 1e-9. The wrong engine sp_slack (the repair removed) is caught by unit tests only.

Contract text of the author that was wrong: rules.hpp (g) and src/forcing.hpp said 'with a continuous column positive only by rounding'. The rounding was that of the sum of the terms of the row plus the error bound of its activity, not of the column that is moved. Both texts are corrected with the code.

The alias is written x = start + scale * x_p without a shift by the lower bound of the binary, so it is right only for a binary with lower bound 0. The author presents the restriction to the bounds 0 and 1 as a numerical choice against rounded offsets; it is also a validity condition of the code as written (his wrong engine sp_unit fails the oracle 1,183 times in 1.2 million models for that reason). No defect while the restriction stands; whoever lifts it must add the shift.

A wrong engine that takes a continuous column with the bounds 0 and 1 as the binary (sp_int_binary) is caught by the oracle on 2 of 4.8 million release models and by one unit test: the generator never draws such a column as the binary of a probing row. A wrong engine that does not list a waiting row again (sp_wait_lost) is caught by no campaign check in 4.8 million models, only by the author's unit test columns_probing_connected_row_without_an_event_is_listed; the events driver of tests/test_columns_events.cpp does not meet the case either.

The slack test of the repair is conservative: in the release campaign of ceb56c208 it leaves 3 rows in 40.8 million models with --probing (profiles default and scaled, seed 44000133455; profile dense, seed 44000226538) where the engine under review made the reduction and the oracle passed. In the one I traced the bound of the continuous column came from bound propagation with an outward slack of about 1e-15 left by an activity that had held a term of 2e15. On the 240 and the 17 local dumps it leaves no row.

Hazard by argument only, not shown by a model, shared with the base: the substitution deletes a coefficient of the root that cancels within tol.cancellation = 1e-12 relative (src/alias_apply.hpp:160). With the scale of simple probing (range up to 1e6) and its size test (coefficient times bound up to 1e8) the deleted coefficient can reach 2e-4 times the binary; the best point I could construct on paper moves a row by about 1.4e-6. The doubleton equations have no size test at all.

Binary check sums are comparable only inside one worktree: the release tools embed one source path (src/state_storage.cpp). The author's SHA-256 9923e92f and mine 39cb1c0f of the same commit differ for that reason; my build of edd147a7e is byte-identical with the build that the first reviewer left, and gives the hash and rounds of the author's stored summaries on all 240 instances in both modes.

Design citations: I checked the ones the author lists against the base commit and they are as he reports (substitute at src/rules_doubleton.cpp:113 and the batch at :208 where the design says 108-160 and 212-243; edge test at src/alias_forest.cpp:41; forest contract at include/gprs/postsolve.hpp:272, not 149-169; rounds at src/presolve.cpp:338; check/structure_check.hpp has 2,076 lines; forcing row at src/rules_rows.cpp:152; HPresolve.cpp:2696-2698 agrees and tests the balance with small_matrix_value). I trusted the code.

Statements of the author that I tested and that hold: 495 tests in both builds; identity with the family off; all 110 wrong engines caught, the six doubleton ones on the moved code among them (on my seeds 97 by a campaign check and 13 by unit tests only, his count was 96 and 14 because ev_unread met one second presolve here); the check tool counts; the reductions; fixed-point flags and rounds.

Process notes of this review: the campaign chain on the commit under review was stopped after its release part (204 million models) so that the assertion part could run on the repaired engine. The identity driver on the 240 dumps ran in the release build with two option variants; with eight variants and phase hashes it takes about an hour per build on one process, and the assertion build on the 240 was not run. The 81 wrong engines that do not concern simple probing ran on 300,000 models each instead of 1.2 million.

assumptions.title: Slack of a continuous column, absolute part (new, this review)
assumptions.statement: For every continuous column j of a probing row and each of the two gaps: (positive part of the gap + error bound of the activity) times the largest coefficient of j in its rows must not exceed |a_j| times (8 rounding units of the term of j there + probing_slack * tol.zero * tol.feasibility). With the default the alias moves no other row of the column by more than 1e-15 beyond the rounding of the column's own term.
assumptions.switch: options_t::probing_slack = 1, in units of tol.zero * tol.feasibility (gprs_presolve --probing-slack); 0 allows the rounding of the term alone, inf is no test
assumptions.alternatives: A larger factor (1e6 gives 1e-9, 1e8 gives 1e-7 per column and row); a form without the largest coefficient, which then needs no limited flag; no test (the commit under review).
assumptions.measured: 240 and 17 local dumps, default and primal-only: no row left, and the reduced-model hash is the same on all 240 with 1, with 0 and with inf. Campaign of ceb56c208: 3 rows left in 204 million release models, 0 in 78 million assertion models. Family of 1,500 slack models: with inf an exact point is lost on 178 (rows read with 1e-6), with 1 on none.

assumptions.title: Slack of a continuous column, relative part (new, this review)
assumptions.statement: A continuous column may sit off its bound by forcing_rounding_units = 8 rounding units of the bound; a row that holds it is then moved by 8 rounding units of the term of the column there, up to 8.9e-9 for a term of 1e7 and 8.9e-8 at the limit of the size test.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: the named constant forcing_rounding_units, shared with the forcing row
assumptions.alternatives: 4 units (what bound propagation moves a bound by); 0.
assumptions.measured: Family of 1,500 slack models: on 20 a row of the reduced model is off by more than 1e-9 and less than 1e-6. Not measured on real instances beyond the equal hashes.

assumptions.title: A row left for the slack test makes the call report limited (new, this review)
assumptions.statement: The slack test reads the other rows of a column, which change without an event of the probing row, so a row left for it alone sets rule_result_t::limited and the result loses the fixed-point flag.
assumptions.alternatives: A column list fed by entry events that brings the row back; a test that reads the row alone.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: no flag lost (234 and 233 as before). Campaign: 3 results in 204 million release models.

assumptions.title: Rounding allowance of the forcing test (changed by this review, commit 458a03aef; forcing row of Stage 1 and simple probing)
assumptions.statement: A set of entries with a continuous column is forcing only when the positive gap is at most the error bound of the activity plus 8 rounding units of the smallest term |a * bound| of a continuous column. Before: 8 rounding units of the sum of all terms.
assumptions.switch: no switch: the named constant forcing_rounding_units
assumptions.alternatives: The sum of the terms (before; reports the model of wrong_results infeasible); the per-column test with the largest coefficient of each column as in simple probing, which needs column scans in the row rules; no allowance.
assumptions.measured: 17 and 240 local dumps, default and primal-only: every field equal to the commit before. Random models: 2.1 million per build with simple probing off equal to the base engine, 2.1 million (release) with it on equal to ceb56c208. Campaign 51 million release and 25.5 million assertion models clean.

assumptions.title: Error bound of an activity as an allowance for a continuous column (not listed by the author)
assumptions.statement: The forcing test adds the error bound to |gap| against the reduction for the tolerance, but allows a positive gap up to the error bound for a continuous column. Next to fixed terms of 1e19 that is 7e-13. In simple probing the slack test now counts the error bound against the reduction; in the forcing row it is still allowed.
assumptions.alternatives: Refuse a row with a continuous column whose activity error bound exceeds a share of the tolerance, as bound propagation does (tol.activity_error_share).
assumptions.measured: Second model of wrong_results. A forcing-row analogue did not reproduce in one try; not measured further.

assumptions.title: A conditional row without any point counts as forcing (not listed by the author as such)
assumptions.statement: A negative gap, the activity beyond the side by up to tol.feasibility * min|a| / max(1, max|a|), passes the forcing test, also next to a continuous column. The value of the binary that has no exact point stays in the reduced model, with the deleted row off by up to that tolerance.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::feasibility; options_t::probing_balance bounds the two gaps together
assumptions.alternatives: Take only gaps that are zero up to rounding.
assumptions.measured: Model in wrong_results (row off by 3e-7 at the kept value). 5,888 perturbed models: nothing beyond 2e-6 gained. How many rows of the 240 fire only through a negative gap: not measured.

assumptions.title: The alias is written for a binary with lower bound 0
assumptions.statement: x = start + scale * x_p has no shift by the lower bound of the binary, so the restriction of the binary to the bounds 0 and 1 is a validity condition of the code, not only a guard against rounded offsets.
assumptions.alternatives: The design's form with (x_p - l_p), for any integer column with bounds one apart.
assumptions.measured: Author's wrong engine sp_unit: oracle 1,183 in 1.2 million models. 240 local dumps: no visit left for it.

assumptions.title: Root of a tree of the batch (not listed by the author)
assumptions.statement: The forest roots a tree at an integer column before a continuous one, then at the column that makes the most edges admissible, then the one with the most live entries, then the smallest index. It decides which column stays, which row keeps a cut edge, and how much the rows of the root fill.
assumptions.alternatives: The binary of the first row of the tree; the column with the fewest entries.
assumptions.measured: not measured (240 local dumps: no cut edge, depth above 1 in 6 calls)

assumptions.title: Bounds transferred to an integer root (moved code, not listed)
assumptions.statement: A transferred bound of an integer root is rounded with tol.feasibility / max(1, |scale|) and 4 rounding units of the bound (transfer_error_units); beyond that the root is tightened, fixed or the model reported infeasible.
assumptions.switch: no switch: named constant transfer_error_units = 4; tolerances_t::feasibility
assumptions.alternatives: The tolerance in row units. With options_t::alias_scale_limit above about 1e10 the slack falls below the rounding of a composed offset; the default 1e6 is safe by a factor of 1e4.

assumptions.title: Cancellation in the substitution (moved code, not listed)
assumptions.statement: A coefficient of the root that the substitution leaves within tol.cancellation = 1e-12 of the sum of the two magnitudes is deleted as a structural zero, and a cost likewise.
assumptions.alternatives: Delete only an exact zero, or below an absolute size times the range of the root.
assumptions.measured: not measured; by argument the deleted coefficient can reach 2e-4 with the scale of simple probing

open: Decision for the owner: whether the forcing-row repair (458a03aef, Stage 1 code) goes in with milestone M2. For: the base engine reports a feasible model infeasible and the repair is a strict tightening with no measured cost. Against: it has the shorter campaign (51 million release, 25.5 million assertion models, against 204 and 78 million for ceb56c208), and 'the off run is identical to M1' then holds by measurement (17 and 240 dumps, 4.2 million random models) and no longer by construction.

The forcing row still allows the error bound of its activity for a continuous column and has no test against the largest coefficient of a column. Simple probing needed both (second model). I found no failing model for the row rules in one try; a rigorous repair needs column scans in the row rules and its own cost review.

For milestone M4: the single-lock alias (R8) must use the per-column slack test of simple probing, not 'the form of the forcing rule (rounding size)' that amendment D, validity item 6, names; that form had this hole. Its scale is upper - lower as well, so it also needs the range test and the size test, which live in the anonymous namespace of src/rules_simple_probing.cpp.

The default of probing_slack (1e-15 beyond the rounding of the term) is the strict choice. It costs nothing on the 257 local instances and 3 reductions in 204 million campaign models; the 44 testbed instances and the node are not measured. The campaign's option draw does not vary it.

Blind spots of the campaign generator, each covered by unit tests only: a slack of rounding size next to a large term or a huge fixed term (outside the oracle class and below its relative 1e-9); a continuous column with bounds 0 and 1 where the binary belongs; a waiting row that the batch leaves without an event (three probing rows, two of them joined through a continuous column).

The tolerance convention of the rule (a conditional row that is off by up to the forcing tolerance, or has no point at all, counts as forcing) is the design's and Stage 1's. Whether a value of the binary without an exact point should stay in the reduced model is a question for the end test with solutions.

Not run: the identity driver on the 240 dumps in the assertion build; the wrong engines through the check tool on real instances; anything with a solver (the verdicts that compare optima are skipped: 352 on the 17 dumps, 4,320 on the 240); the node and the 44 testbed instances; AddressSanitizer.

Merge: the three commits touch src/rules_simple_probing.cpp, src/forcing.hpp, src/presolve.cpp (one line), include/gprs/rules.hpp and presolve.hpp, tools/gprs_fuzz.cpp, gprs_presolve.cpp and run_campaign.sh, analysis/bench240_stage1c.py (one line), check/make_mutants.py (twelve entries appended) and two new test files; nothing in src/rules_parallel_rows.cpp or tests/test_parallel_rows.cpp. The unreviewed merge e3dbc812d contains edd147a7e without them. Expect a conflict at the end of MUTANTS in check/make_mutants.py only.
The stored results gpu_presolve/results/bench240/s1c_m2_mac were not regenerated: the tool's result now has one more field (probing.slack_refused, 0 everywhere) and the hashes are equal.
Known class (b) has a second seed (44600359798 with --probing --singletons, profiles huge_parallel and huge_equations); it still has no owner.
